1.
The appellants / claimants filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act of 1988').

Challenge in this appeal is to the award dated 18/11/2016 passed by the Chief Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raipur, CG in claim case No.111/2012.
2.

entities.text: Chief Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellants / claimants had filed application under Section 166 of the Act of 1988 claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.77,50,000/- on account of death of Girdhar Manwani in an unfortunate accident occurred on 29/02/2012.
The appellants / claimants pleaded that the deceased - Girdhar Manwani was aged about 33 years and his monthly income was Rs.25,000/-.
The accident occurred because of the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.CG 04, HA - 5008.
Respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is owner and the vehicle was insured by respondent No.3/ insurance company.
The claim application was resisted by the respondents-driver, owner and the insurance company.

Learned Tribunal, on the basis of pleadings,
framed as many as 6 issues and decided those issues in favour of the appellants / claimants.
Learned Tribunal was pleased to award total compensation of Rs.27,70,000/- to the appellants / claimants.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants argues that the salary of the deceased was Rs.25,000/-, the amount of compensation awarded on other heads is on the lower side and wrong deduction has been made as the dependents are six in number.

4. Learned counsel for respective respondents support the award and submit that learned Tribunal has rightly assessed the monthly income of the deceased and since the 6th claimant is the father,
1/4th deduction towards personal expenses has been rightly applied.
They further submit that the award on other admissible heads are also justified and just compensation has been awarded.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the records.

sentences.text: 6. The assessment of monthly income by the learned Tribunal appears to be on the lower side.
From perusal of the salary slip issued by the employer (Ex.P/14) clearly goes to show that the total earning of the deceased in the month of February, 2012 was Rs.14584/.

Though there are some deductions,
but they are the deductions towards provident fund and professional tax.

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Indira Srivastava & Ors. reported in (2008) 2 SCC 763, the monthly income of the deceased ought to have been taken as Rs.14584.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, interest @ 6% is also awarded on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of filing of the claim application to be deposited within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
